sources.t: San Francisco Board of Supervisors: legislation records (Legistar), 2014 to November 2026; each row links to its file

tables.how: Every resolution, ordinance or motion about a contract, grant or agreement introduced from January 2014 to 12 November 2026 whose title uses the word retroactive, leaving out acceptances of outside grants, settlements and agreements that pay the City: 297 files worth $7,456,477,180 (the amount after the file, or the increase where no total is stated). Lateness is the days from the start of the term stated in the title to the day the file was introduced; for an amendment it runs from the date the title says the change takes effect, and is blank where the title gives none. It can be measured for 125 files: the middle one is 88 days and 32 are more than 180 days. By department: Public Health 64 of its 269 money files; department not stated in the title 40 of its 325 money files; Airport 38 of its 386 money files; Public Utilities Commission 16 of its 217 money files; Municipal Transportation Agency 16 of its 87 money files; Real Estate Division 15 of its 235 money files. 4 titles name no other party.
tables.limits: Amounts and names are read by rule from each file's title; the link opens the file itself, which governs. A title shows the latest version of the legislation, and a file that states no earlier amount cannot appear here.  Many are late because a grant from the State arrived late, a negotiation ran past the start date, or the Board's own calendar delayed the item; the title does not say which. A file that was late but whose title leaves the word out is missing, and a start date long before the file can be the original term of an agreement that only now needs Board approval.
